messages.text: You still want me to come by Saturday? I can bring the long bit and grab those 2x12s from Lowe's.
Yes. I fixed the cabinet hinge and the loose faucet washer today. I'll leave the garage light and boards for you.
Works. I'll get there before supper so we're not messing with it after the sun drops.
Good. I'll have the step stool and screws laid out, but you can take the tall part.
You still need that socket set Saturday or did Jim find one?
Bring yours if you can. We have two porch rails loose and the ramp boards by the east door need tightening.
I can drop it by Friday night. You hauling cans over too?
Yes, boxed them today. If a family loses a roof or an older fellow runs short, the shelves ought to be ready before they ask.
Karen said there is a supper after the 6 o'clock service Sunday. You staying for it?
If my knee is decent, yes. Last time one fellow brought a steel guitar and they kept it going in the fellowship hall.
Same guy who does those old barroom-truck-stop sounding numbers?
Likely so. He knows Silver Wings and a few from the red book too.
You still coming by after chess to show those fellows the hinge trick?
Yes. I have the little jig in the truck. Then I need to stop at church and look at that loose handrail.
Busy man for somebody who used to say empty mornings were too long.
They are better when somebody is waiting on a tape measure or a bad door.
You coming Tuesday or staying home with those TV fellas talking over each other?
Coming. I shut that mess off after the weather and checked the city posting instead.
Good. Bring that pothole list you mentioned. I want to see if my street made it.
Printed it already. Thirty minutes of TV was plenty for one morning.
You still coming Tuesday? Been saving that corner board by the coffee urn.
I will be there. Been thinking on that dash-cam story you brought up, too.
Good. I said the fellow wearing the badge had a hard call, but the shove after it was over needs more than a shrug.
That is about where I land. Hard job does not make every rough move right.
I can ring after supper tonight if that still works. Also, did the blue tackle box end up in the hall closet?
Tonight is fine. Tackle box is by the back door now.
Good. I will stop by Sunday after lunch and help get those three envelopes addressed before they disappear under your mail stack.
Bring your coffee mug. I found two stamps already.
I put Lucy's birthday pictures where you usually look. The album has 18 photos.
Found them on the blue F page. I saved the one with her holding the cake.
Good. Do not bother with the argument under Uncle Ray's post. It went nowhere.
I looked at the pictures and shut it. That was enough for me.
Wind looks mean Friday. Hefner may be more trouble than fish.
Wind looks mean by noon. Still want Hefner or call it?
Hefner still looks too windy Friday. Also, center desk asked if you want the luncheon form turned in with mine.
I saw that. Might drive by Arcadia anyway if the knee lets me sit awhile.
Call it. I will use the morning to sharpen that old auger and drop the spare latch at Mrs. Givens's back gate.
Hold off on fishing. For the form, copy my old county and state lines from last year and leave the DD-214 spot empty again.
Coffee at 6:30 if we go. If not, keep that workbench busy.
You still using that beat-up red toolbox?
Got it. Same as the last folder, no extra papers stapled to it.
That is the plan. Supper, dishes, then the little Chevy kit for an hour.
It opens, closes, and has what I need. New paint would not tighten one screw.
That mower still coughs when it gets warm. You ever shim the choke plate on those?
Check the linkage first. If you head this way from Norman Saturday, bring it and we can look.
Might do that. Also, that late OKC tip tonight worth staying up for?
I'll catch the first half and see. These 8:30 starts are getting ambitious.
Dad, on that tag office form, do they want your current city or the old one too?
Same answer either way. Oklahoma City has been the line on those papers every time I've filled them out.
Figures. I found the 1953 folder in the drawer with the truck title stuff.
Leave it on the kitchen table when you come by. I still need those old papers for Karen.
Before you take the Chevy that far, want me to look at belts and hoses Saturday?
That would help. I have Oklahoma City to Tucumcari penciled for the first day, but I may stop sooner if the knee gets stiff.
Found that little tape recorder in a box at the shop. You still want one for your old stories?
Yes. My hand gets tired after two pages. I can talk through the farm years while I sort the spring folder.
Send me the towns when you settle them. I can mark a couple parts stores along I-40.
I will. I am still matching the rooms to what is already in the travel envelope.
I can bring it Sunday. Also I can fix that porch latch while I'm there.
Bring the recorder, leave the latch to me unless I holler. I already bought the screws.
Found that flat box in the garage rafters. Had Ray's name on masking tape and a stack of black-and-white pictures.
Set it by the kitchen table. I want to put dates and names on the backs before they get mixed in.
There was also a book with Eisenhower on the cover tucked in there. Yours?
Yes. Ray marked two pages years ago. I may copy one line for the grandchildren folder.
Wind looks ugly for Hefner. If we still go, bring that old black camera; the herons were close to the bank last time.
I already have the F2 body by the door. If we get skunked, I can at least bring home a few frames.
Fine by me. I want a copy after you get them off the card. Label it Hefner so I can find it.
I put them under the day first, then the lake name. Keeps me from hunting all over the computer.
Wind lays down before sunup Friday. Hefner looks better than Arcadia this time.
I can be there at 6:20 if my knee wakes up right. I still have the small tackle box in the trunk.
I'll bring minnows and coffee. Don't let Earl keep you out too late moving pieces tonight.
He already took one rook off me. I'll turn in early after supper.
Could you look over the ramp screws before Saturday? I can meet you at the church closet at 8:15.
I can. I already sorted the bits and put fresh tape on the cords after Wednesday.
Thank you. The younger guys listen better when you show them the slow way first.
I will keep it simple: pre-drill, brace the board, glasses on before anyone touches the trigger.
Wind is supposed to get ugly tonight. I am calling off Hefner in the morning.
Good call. I already topped off the truck and put the little bills back by the flashlight.
That is more organized than me. I just found my lantern under a tackle box.
I checked the bank sheet too. That 400 mark is still sitting where it belongs.
Milton, I found the church receipt envelope from the ramp repair morning. Do you still need the hardware slips?
Yes, please. I put $118.64 on my card for screws, sealant, and two sanding pads.
I will bring them Sunday. We can reimburse what the church used and leave your own supplies separate.
That helps. I already marked the month at $2,250 because the shop shelf and one annual bill landed together.
Wind looks mean at Hefner. You still want to stop by Delma's after bait?
Bait yes. Delma's no this morning. I packed coffee and two containers from last night's pot.
You passing up that Friday plate? I may need to mark the calendar.
You see that north wind yet? Hefner may be a mess by eight.
Not passing it up forever. Just not every time they hang that sign by the door.
Just poured the first mug and had the radar up. Let me step out back and see what it is doing here.
Wind looks low Friday. Hefner before sun gets too high?
Works for me if I can swing by Crest and the tag office on the same run.
No hurry. If the flags are snapping at your place, I am staying home.
Bring coffee. I'll bring minnows if you are skipping the counter breakfast.
Flags moving some. Beds are damp from last night too, so I am voting no for this morning.
I'll pack biscuits. Had the plumber here yesterday, so the skillet wins this week.
You still got those tiny axle pins from the old Ford box?
Found two in the coffee can. Need them after I trim the running boards.
Use the sharp blade. That soft wood tears if you rush it.
I am not rushing today. Just keeping my hands busy before Karen gets here.
You still coming by Sunday dinner? Lisa sent me some video saying skip the pharmacy stuff and drink tonic water.
Dinner yes. That video can stay where it is. I checked Dr. Henson's portal note and the CDC page instead.
You still got that little Briggs carb trick you showed me? Mower at the shop is flooding.
Check the float first. Same thing we did on those yard machines after I started with Cline's crew.
Figured. Just wanted to know before Mom starts asking everybody.
Tell her I already asked the pharmacist Thursday. Sore arm, no drama.
That was right after your class picture in the blue gown, wasn't it?
Pretty close. I had sawdust on my boots before that summer got hot.
Dad, after coffee today I found the old envelope with your ticket receipt and insurance card copies. Do you still need it?
Keep it with the car papers. That was from the stop on May Avenue when the taillight was out.
I figured. It was just the repair note and that written warning, nothing else.
That sounds right. The man was plain with me, I got it fixed, and that was the end of it.
Dad, I found two photo sleeves under the insurance folder. One says Sedona in your handwriting and the other just says Kansas hills.
I can stop by after church and sort that blue binder with you. Did the county paper go behind the insurance tab or the utility tab?
Leave those on the dining table, please. I was comparing the red rock shadows with the grass ridge shots.
County paper is loose on the kitchen table. Insurance is behind the green divider. I had the Ace receipt in an envelope, unless I carried it to the garage.
I will. The newer card from Friday is beside them too, still in the little black case.
Leave it all where it is. I will bring sticky notes and we can match the envelopes to the check register.
Good. Those Friday frames may help me decide what light to wait for next time.
Good. The bank only needs my regular checking statement for this one, so there should not be another packet to hunt down.
I can come by after church if you want help with receipts. Did you already set up the little case by the coffee maker for the week?
I can help sort the mail after coffee. Did the insurance envelope end up on the desk or under those little plane boxes?
I did it after breakfast. Monday through Saturday are full.
Desk, I think. I put the wing pieces on the spare bed and lost the envelope under the cutting mat.
Good. Please keep the refill paper on the counter so I do not accidentally throw it in the mail stack.
I will bring a folder. Please do not let me pay any of those for you. I am only helping find the papers.
Folder is fine. The drafts come out of my checking like always.
It is under the sugar bowl. The small white one is in the first morning slot.
Morning, Milton. I added the repair-day supply list to the church page last night.
I saw it after breakfast. I wrote down 2 boxes of screws and the folding table.
Thank you. If the comments drift again, just call me about supplies.
That's what I do. I need the notice, not the back-and-forth.
Milton, could you send me the names you have so far before Wednesday evening?
Yes. I have them in one place now. I am adding the notes on ladders and cordless drills before I send it.
Good. Also put wax rings, Teflon tape, and two 8-foot boards on the materials page if they are not already there.
They are on there. I will email the clean copy tonight so you can run it off at the office.
I found the ramp photo from the spring you first came out with your toolbox.
That was a rough spring. Better to hold a saw than sit around chewing on old papers.
You said back then a steady third chair at the kitchen table might have saved some shouting.
I was too proud and too private. I can see it clearer now.
You bringing that folded county sheet Tuesday, or are we pretending chess is the only thing on the table?
I'll bring it. Still sorting the judge retention notes and that road question. The wording is slippery.
Figured you would have three pencil marks and a complaint about the fine print.
Fine print is where they hide the bill. I want patrols covered and potholes fixed, but they can tell us where the money goes.
Wind looks wrong for Hefner this morning. You still messing with those pepper starts before coffee?
Moved the peppers by the south window and tied up two tomato cages. Sitting more than bending today.
Smart. Bring that little folding seat out there before you get stubborn.
Already by the bean row. I may give the lettuce one mist and quit before I drown it again.
You doing those hall laps before I get there, or am I catching you fresh at the chess table?
I am going early. Dr. Patel circled that part on my paper, so I am trying not to skip Tuesdays.
Use the west door. Less stairs, and I do not want excuses when I beat you.
West door it is. My fingers need a few minutes before they push pawns anyway.
Same table this morning? I saved the corner one before the domino crowd spreads out.
I'll be there by 9:30. Bring that queen-side trick again and I'll be ready.
Sam said you two were talking Arcadia before breakfast Friday. Hope you don't blame the lake when I beat you today.
If I lose, I'll blame the coffee. See you shortly.
You skipping chess again for that faucet-and-ladder crowd?
Only the first game. They asked me to go over extension cords before lunch and I promised I would.
Bring your board after. I want proof you still remember how knights move.
I will be there by 2 if nobody jams another hinge.
For Saturday, can you put Al and Denise on the back steps and keep the younger guys on the fence panels?
I will. I counted eight work gloves, three paint trays, and four sacks of rice for the west table.
Good. Also, Mr. Haney asked if you were still calling tomorrow.
Four o'clock like always. If that storm line comes through south of Moore, tell folks to call me before they wait around.
You want me to bring those mower belts Saturday?
Yes. I am at the kitchen table with my second cup and the hourly pulled up. Saturday looks dry after nine.
Good. I can swing by after the parts counter opens.
Works. I will check the beds after sunrise and see if the ground firms up.
You want me to bring that newer cordless set Sunday? Mine has two batteries.
You still need that mower belt? I can check the bin after work.
Bring yourself. My old Makita still turns if I charge it overnight.
Yes, but wait until I know the price. I already mapped tomorrow for the belt place, bank, and the lake road.
Karen said the school raffle wanted a gift card from you. She can pick one up.
Tell her I will send cash in an envelope, same as I told her Monday. Put my name small.
Lake road makes sense. No reason to cross town twice.
Exactly. Beans are soaking, so I won't be stopping at Ray's after the belt.
I can come by after work. Want me to grab anything from the corner place?
No need. I have greens warming and a skillet of bread in the oven.
You got tartar sauce in there too or are you behaving?
One small fillet from the freezer. The rest is going in containers before I sit down.
Need that folding table Saturday or is it still buried in the little paint room?
You watch that late game or shut it down?
Still buried. I have the B-25 drying on it and tax papers spread on the other end.
Shut it down. Evenings have been dragging, so I put the radio on and sorted screws for the Bel Air.
No rush. You want me to bring anything when I come by?
No, just yourself. I have the house set the way I like it and the bills covered.
Better than yelling at the TV. Need me to look at that mower Saturday?
No rush. I am all right, just slower after supper. Morning and afternoon were fine.
You going to the school game Friday or saving your grumbling for the TV?
TV sounds better. By the time they kick off, my chair starts looking smarter than the bleachers.
Fine, then keep Sunday open. Dallas will give us enough to argue about.
I'll be ready. You bring the bad takes and I'll bring the coffee.
For the church work morning, could you take the loose cabinet pulls and pantry shelf pegs?
Those are fine. Put me down for the hand tools table too.
Good. I'll have Roy take the roof vent and the breaker room list.
Thank you. I can sort screws, patch the low shelf, and mark what Roy needs.
We may take bottled water to Mrs. Halley if the power flickers again. Do you need anything before I head that way?
I am set here. Batteries, radio, and a few small bills in the drawer.
Good. I will call if she needs help with that porch light.
If it is under 400, I can handle a supply run and settle it after Sunday.
Milton, thank you for staying after the pantry shelf job. Mr. Alvarez said your patient way with the level helped him.
Glad he came. I told him the trick is to mark twice and breathe once.
That line would work well at the center next Thursday too.
Put me down. Thursdays are better when there is a bench full of tools waiting.
Wind looks mean at Hefner. Want to skip bait today?
Skip it. I would rather keep the $18 in the jar after that $407 bill cleared.
Fair. Arcadia can wait until the gusts quit.
Good. The second bank line does not show until next Friday, so I am keeping errands tight.
Wind is 18 by noon. Hefner will be rough.
Saw the same on the county weather page. Turned the TV off before they got to arguing.
Arcadia Saturday then?
Works. I will check the lake notice Friday night and leave the rest alone.
Wind looks tolerable Friday at Arcadia if you still have a young helper riding along.
Looks that way. Dropping a sleeping bag in the spare room Thursday night so we can leave before sunup.
I will bring minnows and coffee. Text me if Karen changes the pickup plan.
Will do. She is calling later to settle the timing.
Do you still need my impact driver Saturday or did somebody else bring one?
Bring yours. The row beside your name is still blank for bits, so toss in the Phillips set too.
Got it. You want me there at 8 or after the first coffee run?
8 if you can. I printed the first page, but I need to add your driver and bits when I get home.
I put the Edmond school office printout in your mail tray. It has the board race notes and the bond totals you asked about.
Thank you. I don't mind paying for roofs and buses if the numbers are plain and somebody is watching the receipts.
That sounds like you. Do you still want me to check the courthouse site for the two names you circled?
Yes. I have one marked from the red flyer but I want the record first.
Milton, do you still have the lumber receipt from the ramp patch? I can turn in the church copy Monday.
I put church slips in a small white envelope. Mine for the back steps went into the house folder, if it stayed there.
No hurry. If Karen is helping with papers Sunday, she may spot it before I do.
I also need to copy the March utility checks while the folder is open.
Milton, I can print those highway pages after pantry setup Sunday if you still need them.
Thank you. I only need the pages for the days I have rooms picked, plus the church office number on the top.
Bring the list. I will make two copies.
I am waiting on one room to come down ten dollars before I write that day in ink.
Wind looks bad for Hefner. You want to move coffee to Monday?
Monday works. I have the Saturday ramp crew, then Sunday morning and the meal after.
That the place with the piano books and the fellow who sings those Bakersfield-sounding tunes?
Yes. He makes those old numbers sound about right after everybody finishes eating.
Karen found Grandpa Wells' photo in that uniform trunk. You keeping the ribbons or should I toss the broken frame?
Keep the photo. The ribbons were his, not mine. My folder for the center just needs license, county certificate, and Medicare card.
Alright. I will bring the trunk Sunday and leave your paperwork stack alone.
Thanks. The family tree page still starts with the Wells and Parkers around Guthrie, so don't mix it into the center papers.
You skipping chess after that insurance mess yesterday?
Going to stay home this morning. The little coupe roof needs fitting and that takes a steady hand.
Better than letting me beat you in four moves.
Give me a week. I may bring the hood piece for you to look at.
You leaving that thick Grant book at the center again Tuesday, or did you finally finish it?
Finished the Vicksburg part. The notes are better than the ballgame was.
Bring the page you said Ray would argue with. I want to hear why.
I copied it beside one of the fishing pictures so the kids know the story behind that summer.
Mom said she can bring the plates for Caleb's birthday if you still want her by Brian.
That's fine. Put me near the coffee and Linda wherever she is comfortable.
Thank you. The kids like not having to run two little parties.
Sixteen years is long enough to pass the potatoes at one table.
Dad, I found the gray Seagate case on the shelf by the printer. Do you still need it Sunday?
Yes. I finally emptied the March card and want to put the Hefner and church hallway sets somewhere besides the desktop.
I will set it with your mail so we do not forget. You had three folders open when I stopped by: 2026-03-04 Hefner, 2026-03-09 History Center, and 2026-03-12 Church.
That sounds right. I get behind and then have to sort the whole batch at once.
One of the pantry ladies asked me about that shared post claiming lemon peel clears everything by Easter. I told her I would not pass it around.
Good. I would rather point folks to the county clinic notice or have them call their doctor's office.
That is about what I told her. Are you still able to help with the ramp after your arm settles?
Yes. It was just tender from Thursday. I can hold boards, maybe not swing hard.
Wind looks mean at Hefner. If we still go, I can wait till 6:30.
Make it 6:30. I need coffee and the Saturday slot first.
Fine by me. Bring the refill slip if we pass Walgreens on the way back.
I put it in my shirt pocket so I remember.
Wind is too hard for a boat this morning. You still going out with that camera before coffee?
I might. Low sun on those open fields east of Jones can be worth the cold hands.
You and that sunrise business. Save some patience for the big hole in Arizona.
That one will need more than patience. I want to be standing there before the buses show up.
You survive all those candles yesterday, or do I get an easy chess win Tuesday?
Karen wouldn't let them all on the cake. Said the smoke alarm had enough work already.
At 73, you can demand a bigger cake. Senior center owes you one too.
Just bring your queen out too early again and we'll call it even.
Dad, I found the envelope from your guidance office while sorting the cabinet. It has the blank application pages and your final transcript.
Leave it in the folder. I remember Mrs. Haney saying I could send those in, but Mr. Cline needed a helper Monday morning.
I will keep it with the old pay stubs and the photo of you holding that tool belt.
That belt saw doors, drywall patches, and plenty of leaky sinks.
I can stop by after church. Do you want me to move the potting mix bags off the porch?
Yes, just set them near the raised bed. I put the knee brace on before messing with the lettuce tray.
Please keep the hose light on that tray. Last Sunday it looked more like soup than soil.
Fair. The tomatoes and green beans can wait until morning anyway.
Dad, I put the new batteries in the arm cuff and left the little log beside your coffee tin.
Found it. I wrote this morning's numbers after I got back from the center.
Good. Please keep using the side entrance when your knees are touchy, and turn the phone up when I call tonight.
Call before 7 if you can. After that I am usually done answering much.
For Saturday, would you rather check supply lists or work on the ramp rail with Carl?
Put me with Carl. I can still measure straight, and that ramp story belongs in my summer stack after I get home.
Done. I will keep the lifting to the younger backs.
Fair. Just don't park me at the sign-in table all morning.
Senior center posted that Tuesday chess is moved to Room B. You see it?
Yes. Same place I check the lunch menu. I marked Room B.
Do not read below it unless you want your blood up. Folks are hollering again.
No need. I got the room number and closed it.
Checking in before the school phones get busy. Did the three cards make it into the mailbox?
Yes, and I put a note in each like you said.
Good. I will call Thursday evening too. Sunday may be shorter, but I can still come by with the folder.
That works. I saved the insurance paper on the kitchen table.
I put your tax folder back on the hall table. It has SSA-1099, bank interest, the church mileage notes, and the supply receipts.
Good. I still need to add the March 7 lumber receipt and the box of masks.
I did not see any other forms come in. If one shows up late, leave it clipped to the front.
That should be all of it. The rest is just the center and church pile.
We have the pantry shelves to tighten Friday if your knee is up to it. No pressure.
I can do the lower shelf and sit between turns. Being around the crew will do me good.
Good. Come early and we can have a quiet word before the others arrive.
I would like that. I have kept my mornings steady, but those dark supper hours still stretch out.
Chess Tuesday, unless you're off chasing that porch leak again.
I'll be there. I put sealant on the lower corner this morning. The shingles can wait for the fellow Karen gave me.
Smart enough. We can argue Cowboys at 10 like civilized men.
Make it 10. I don't want to be crossing town late after your victory speech.
A few folks may be heated again Sunday. Could you sit near Earl and help keep the table steady?
I can do that. I would rather hear folks out in that room than go stand downtown with a sign.
That is what I hoped. We can say a uniform does not excuse a bad hand without turning the whole hour sour.
Yes. Let the facts come out, and if someone crossed a line, there ought to be consequences.
You skipping chess Tuesday for another porch job?
Only if the trim board comes in. I told Jim I would measure twice before he orders.
You and that little pencil behind your ear. At least let them buy lunch.
Coffee is plenty. If the door shuts square, that is enough.
You sounded shorter on the phone earlier. Did you get outside after supper?
I did. The television crowd had me wound up, so I clicked it off and walked to the mailbox.
Good. I can bring the school bond packet Sunday if you still want the actual figures.
Bring it. I would rather read the numbers than hear folks bark about it.
Wind is ugly at Hefner. You want to call off the lake and keep your lumber run?
Yes. Pastor Jim needs trim cut for the back hallway, and I promised the center I would bring the clamp set.
You have more places expecting you than fish do.
That has turned out to be a good thing.
Leaving the Norman shop around noon. I can drop by with that carb if you still want to hear it.
Come on. We can put it on the bench before the OKC game.
Works. I need to be back before dark, but I can stay through lunch.
That's plenty. Better than trying to start anything after supper.
You skipping Tuesday chess to stare at maps again?
Only after lunch. I found a cheaper room on the east side of Albuquerque if the wind is not ugly that afternoon.
That is a lot of checking for one bed and a TV.
One bad stop makes the next morning hard. I also need the day's towns written clear enough for Karen.
I am filling the clinic history page before I come by. For birthplace I used Oklahoma City like your certificate says.
That is right. For the old address section, it should be Oklahoma City, Midwest City, and the Norman apartment from when Brian was little.
Okay. I will leave the uniform-paper number line blank and bring the German-English family sheet back with your receipts.
I can come by after lunch Sunday and help with the captions under those scanned pictures.
Good. I have Ray in the lake picture, but I need you to check the cousins' names.
Please put the little lesson notes in your plain words. The grandkids will read those more than dates.
I marked one from the Lincoln book about temper. It fits that summer better than anything I could invent.
Karen asked if you still have that 2009 courthouse envelope. Mom's copy is missing a page.
I have the blue folder. Only other county paper in there is the 1978 certificate.
Bring it Saturday? Linda said no rush, just before the tax papers get sorted.
I'll put it with Caleb's card and keep it out of the cake frosting.
I put the insurance packet by your coffee tin. It still has Oklahoma City printed in both address boxes.
I put the insurance form on top of the mail pile. Do you want me to fill in the easy parts before I leave?
That saves me writing it twice. They ask the same questions every year.
No, sit with your coffee. I want to keep my own hand on those papers while I can.
Also, the copy I need shows 3/14 and 1953, but the corner is torn. I'll tape it before I scan it.
Thanks. Leave it with the receipts and I'll sign whatever page you marked.
All right. I did find three photos in the receipt box, one fishing and two from the old shop.
Good. Put fishing in fall and the shop ones in summer. I need them before I rewrite that part.
Milton, would you mind helping set the chairs back after tonight's meal? The youth moved them for practice.
I can. Leave me by the piano side if they pass out the old books.
I heard Walt may bring the Telecaster again, so you may get your porch-swing songs.
That suits me. I was raised on Sunday nights that ended just that way.
You still want me to look at that loose gutter Saturday?
Yes. I bought brackets at Lowe's and wrote the amount on the March sheet, but the little slip is not in the glove box now.
Check the coffee can on the workbench. You put small papers there when you empty your pockets.
If we find it, I will put it behind the insurance page with the roof and water-heater papers.
You coming to chess today or still hiding from my queen?
Coming. Missed two Tuesdays and my game is probably rusty.
Good. I saved your chair. Cowboys talk is extra.
I need the chair and the talk. Knee is better, and getting out beats staring at the back door after supper.
Chess is at noon. If I win fast, we can hit Ruby's before the crowd.
Win first, then maybe. I brought a jar of soup so I don't order half the board.
You and that soup jar. Ruby's has the corn squares today.
That is why the jar is in my bag.
You coming to chess or did that forwarded chart scare you off from everything with a needle?
Chess at two. The chart looked like somebody made it during halftime.
Ha. I only sent it because Roy was waving it around.
I will stick with Dr. Henson and the county page. Bring your Cowboys excuses.
You left your pencil by the board again. I handed it to the desk lady.
Thanks. I was hurrying because Sam called about Arcadia and the morning weather.
Tell him not to steal my Tuesday opponent. I need someone who falls for that bishop fork.
I'll be back next Tuesday unless the rain changes everything.
Wind is ugly this morning. Hefner can wait. You still stopping by the precinct before coffee?
Yes. I want to get there early, then we can sit at Braum's and complain about the lake.
Take your cheat sheet. Last time you had more notes than bait.
It's in my jacket. I left one line blank until I read the budget answer again. No free pass just because the mailer had my usual color.
You coming Tuesday or did the yard steal you again?

Radar says the rain holds off. I will be there before the first board is set up.
Do you want me to pick up anything before Sunday, or are you doing your north-side rounds?

That sounds fine. I can still bring soup if the tire bill made this week awkward.
I've got chili and cornbread. Tell the kids we can do cake here instead of Ted's this time.
Maddie asked if you ever open the little camera app she put on your phone.
Hardly. I tapped it today and it wanted some new code. The blue F one still shows your pictures and the church note fine.
She can fix it Sunday if you want. She mostly hoped you could see her track meet pictures there too.
Sunday is fine. I already saw the family ones you put up, and Sam's storm update came through the usual page.
When I visit Sunday, I will bring soup and look over that clinic form if you still need me to.
Thanks. The form asks for a few morning readings, so I wrote them on the pad by the case.
That works. Leave the empty refill bag there too, and I will staple everything together.
It is all beside the coffee maker. Sunday through Wednesday are set already.
Milton, the Thursday room is open if you still want to hear the woman from Norman show her Route 66 slide work before repair day planning.
I can come. I want to ask how she keeps track of towns when she scans a whole roll.
Good. Bring your little notebook. If you carry that old camera, I will save you a chair near the aisle.
I may bring it. I still need to copy last Sunday's hallway shots off the machine before I make another mess.
We can use another pair of hands on the ramp boards Friday. Still all right if I drop the screws by your place first?
Yes. Leave them by the front door if I am in the back room with the magnifier lamp on.
I remember. Narrow path between the desk and the little shelves.
That path stays narrow because nobody else has to use it. I keep it working for me.
You need my cordless saw Saturday or are you set?
Bring it if you come by. The church door frame is swollen, and Monday I am showing the center group how to square one.
You sound busier now than when you punched a clock.
Different kind of busy. It sits better.
You skipping chess Tuesday to play foreman again?
Only the morning. Jim has me matching names to ladders and sorting the canned stuff after lunch.
That from the wind damage out by Del City?
Some of it. When somebody's place gets hit or an old neighbor can't get out, sitting on our hands is no plan.
You coming Tuesday, or are you hiding from my queen's gambit again?
I will be there. Had a plumber look at the back hose bib, but the number came in below my 400 line.
Good. Bring your board if the center's lights blink like last time.
Board is in the car. Lantern and the cash pouch are by the hall closet if the weather turns first.
The plumber called back. He can look at the gas line to the dryer Monday at 8:30.
Take that slot. I cleaned the lint trap housing and tightened the loose shelf beside it, but I did not touch the line.
Good. Do you want me to stop by Sunday and move the storage tubs away from the dryer?
Yes, please. I can label the boxes and clear the small stuff before you get here.
The school office has extra tickets for tonight's 7:30 game. Do you want me to leave one on your porch?
No, thank you. I'll listen from the kitchen and save my legs for tomorrow.
All right. Brian said he may call after he closes up, unless Dallas talk with Earl wears you out first.
Have him call. Engines before scores if he's got another puzzle.
The receipt envelope made it back to my desk. Do you want it Sunday or should I leave it in your box?
Leave it in my box, please. I still need to enter the $38.74 for screws and the two toilet parts.
I also have three more men asking about the April work morning. Same way as last time?
Yes, have them email me. Once I have their tools and hours, I will print a fresh page.
For Saturday's repair list, the pantry desk asked whether you want the old-timers parking tag like Frank uses.
No tag for me. I will park by the ramp and bring the drill. My papers are just the regular church volunteer ones.
Understood. I have you down with the local phone, Oklahoma City certificate copy, and the Wells family contact sheet.
That is enough. I can be there by 8 if the rain holds off.
Milton, Mrs. Hanley asked if you had any extra tomato cages before Saturday's repair day.
I can spare two after I finish tying the peppers. They are by the shed next to the flower flats.
Thank you. Take the stool with you if you are working low. No rush on our end.
Will do. I already learned not to kneel long after fooling with that wet lettuce bed.
Milton, the fellowship hall board still has room for three more framed pictures after Sunday.
Karen said the afternoon got heavy. No need to call back tonight unless you want to.
I can bring the Sedona red wall, one Flint Hills rise, and maybe that Oklahoma grass line from last week.
Thank you. I laid out the walnut strips and the grille for that '49 pickup. That will do me better than talking for now.
That will fit well. The one you told me about wanting someday, with first light over the rim, can be the empty spot for now.
Leave me a small space then. I still mean to fill it.
Understood. Slow work and quiet can be useful. I will check in after service Sunday.
Milton, thank you for looking over the pantry closet door. The latch and trim already close better.
It was just a shim and a little sanding. I learned more that first year carrying lumber than I did sitting with those forms from Mrs. Haney.
Karen said she found the old papers for your file. I can copy the Class of '65 page Sunday if you bring it.
I'll bring it after service. The fence sketch from Cline's job is tucked in there too.
Wind is low. Still want the Hefner path before coffee?
Wind's light at Hefner. You still leaving from the same Oklahoma City driveway, or did Karen talk you into Edmond yet?
Yes, but the flat side. Patel's sheet says I need steady minutes, not heroics.
Same driveway. She can ask again when I hit 74.
Wind looks mean at Hefner. Arcadia may be kinder if you still want to fool with bait.
Flat side it is. I will park close so you are not messing with the curb.
Fair enough. I'll grab bait and coffee. You bring that old tackle box.
Arcadia is fine. I need a quiet morning after all that talk at Jim's table.
Appreciate it. I will bring the little notebook and we can sit after one round.
Earl said you kept it calm. Same story as your taillight stop, I guess: answer plain, keep your hands visible, get home.
That is the only way I know. Still, when a recording shows someone went too far, it should not get swept under the rug.
I sorted the receipts you left by the coffee pot. Do you want the yellow sheet updated before I go?
Please. Most months that sheet sits around $1,900 to $2,100, but March is still showing $2,250.
I see the big insurance slip and the workbench pile. The deposits side shows $1,843 plus $620.
That sounds right. Next month should look plainer if I leave the tool aisle alone.

I will stop by Ace tomorrow and square it. I only used one.

Good. His has the bigger pieces. I saved the plain bowl for me.

events.title: Kettle, radar, back beds
events.notes: Grind beans before the kettle. Check OKC hourly and wind. Look at tomato stakes and porch pots before breakfast.

events.title: Early light test roll
events.notes: Bring Nikon, wide lens, spare card. Try the same settings I marked for that canyon rim idea. Watch wind over the grass.

events.title: Walgreens pickup before coffee
events.notes: Bring refill slip. Move new tablets into the Sunday-Saturday case when home.

events.title: Desk-room receipts and March drafts
events.notes: Match OG&E, water, Cox, and insurance receipts to bank drafts. Move airplane kit boxes off the chair before Karen comes Sunday.

events.title: Ledger check after Treasury deposit
events.notes: Treasury line posted: $1,843. Keep March ordinary column near $1,950 before Saturday groceries and gas.

events.title: Print inbox names and March tab
events.notes: Move Sunday replies into the March sheet; mark ladders, drills, and who can lift boards.

events.title: Tuesday laps before chess
events.notes: Bring cane, water, and small notebook for arm-cuff numbers. Take the inside route if the front steps are stiff on the knees.

events.title: Hefner lap: Homeland, library drop, Aldi
events.notes: Thermos in truck. Use freezer stew tonight after OG&E posts.

events.title: Sort old work folder
events.notes: Pull tax box: contractor-helper stubs, first crew photo, 12th-grade transcript copy, notes on door trim and fence receipts.

events.title: Credit union stop
events.location: Tinker Federal Credit Union, Oklahoma City
events.notes: Update ledger. Leave the 400 line alone. Ask for small bills for the kitchen tin before the rain Friday.

events.title: Table with Earl
events.notes: Bring small board clock; call Sam afterward about Friday water and wind.

events.title: Pantry run + supper prep
events.notes: Beans, greens, chicken thighs, cornmeal. Put cafe receipt in March envelope. Save fish plate for Friday, one piece only.

events.title: Bench: sand Chevy fenders
events.notes: Phone on kitchen counter. Thin basswood, 400 grit, leave grille pieces alone until glue sets.

events.title: Back beds: tomato cages, pepper stakes, bean string
events.notes: Use folding stool for the lower row. Check lettuce soil by finger first, then short hose only if dry. Leave space by marigolds.

events.title: Tool table setup and two demos
events.location: Will Rogers Activity Center, Room B
events.notes: Bring eye shields, outlet tester, stripped screw board, sign-in sheet, and extra pencils. Leave afternoon open for cleanup if the drill station runs long.

events.title: Blue folder copies for Karen
events.notes: Pull 1978 county certificate with Linda's name, 2009 judge packet, and seating note for Caleb's cake table.

events.title: Mark sample sheet before recycling mail stack
events.notes: Look up two judge names, county question wording, school millage line, and the street repair item. Compare the tax estimate note with last year's bill.

events.title: County envelope + blue binder
events.notes: Put county notice with insurance renewal page, OG&E bill, water bill, and March repair slips. Check porch drawer for the hardware store ticket before Karen comes Sunday.

events.title: Walgreens counter - ask about spring booster
events.notes: Bring Medicare card. Ask pharmacist whether Dr. Henson's note matches the CDC page Karen printed.

events.title: Mr. Haney
events.notes: Ask whether the walker screw held. Mention extra soup cans from the hallway shelves.

events.title: Morning TV, then off
events.notes: Weather, traffic, OKC bulletin page, county road update.

events.title: Edmond North vs. Memorial score check
events.notes: 7:00 kickoff. Leave bleachers to Karen's crew; check radio and final score after dishes. Cowboys draft show replay at 8:00 if game drags.

events.title: Ramp board swap - Mrs. Alvarez
events.notes: Bring level, drill bits, 2x6 offcuts from shed. Check rail bolts. Leave porch swept before heading out.

events.title: Ramp boards and latch demo
events.location: First Baptist work shed / OKC community room
events.notes: Pick up 2x6 boards before 8:30. Bring spare hinges and small level for the 10:45 door-latch table.

events.title: Brian stop by: garage light and Lowe's boards
events.location: Milton's house; Lowe's on NW Expressway
events.notes: Before Brian arrives: mailbox latch, kitchen drawer slide, coffee ready. Brian: fixture above garage door, attic access panel, 2x12s from pickup. Wrap up before 5:00.

events.title: Karen - coffee, receipts, card envelopes
events.notes: Set out stamps, school photos, and tackle box latch. Check spare-room sheets if Friday morning lake plan holds.

events.title: Evening service and covered-dish supper
events.notes: Bring green beans. Ask song leader whether the red book is out; stay if the guitar circle starts after plates are cleared.

events.title: Desk time: pages + bill stack
events.notes: Winter folder: Tulsa move, hospital nights, Linda leaving. Pay gas bill before Karen comes by; replace porch bulb after lunch.

events.title: Grand Canyon folder: westbound notes
events.notes: Check I-40 wind forecast; compare Tucumcari, Gallup, and Flagstaff room rates; add two longer leg-stretch stops; update Karen's day sheet after choosing towns.

events.title: County records office - certified copy
events.location: Oklahoma County Clerk, 320 Robert S Kerr Ave
events.notes: Bring license, $15 fee, Linda's old folder. Ask for 1951 certificate copy; use same spelling as Wells family papers.

events.title: Kitchen table sorting: Ray box + grandchildren pages
events.notes: Scan 6 photos, write names in pencil first, pull the Truman chapter with the margin note.

events.title: Dishes, Psalm reading, bench time
events.notes: Heat pad before stairs. Call one person if the house feels too still. Finish rear axle on the model.

events.title: Evening program: Tulsa street scenes, 1968-1975
events.location: Oklahoma History Center, 800 Nazih Zuhdi Dr
events.notes: Bring small notebook. Ask whether old Nikkor glass needs adapter notes for scanned files.

events.title: Talk after evening study
events.notes: Bring coffee. Listen first. Ask Jim about the city meeting comments and the video everyone mentioned Sunday.

events.title: Check lake wind, center board, church note
events.notes: Use usual blue F shortcuts before calling Sam. Ignore hot-comment thread if it is still up.

events.title: Family lunch - cake after
events.notes: Karen bringing candles; Brian picking up stew containers. Keep chairs on the porch if weather holds.

events.title: Beans, hourly, seedlings
events.notes: Use the small scoop plus one extra. Check overnight low and rain chance. Lift row cover if the back bed stayed warm.

events.title: Morning numbers and tablet
events.notes: Log cuff reading before coffee. Check Thursday compartment after.

events.title: Treasurer office check
events.notes: Verify spring amount, print confirmation, file with deed copy and insurance declarations. No escrow stub in folder. Add OG&E and water totals to March sheet.

events.title: One loop: pharmacy, bank, Hefner benches, WinCo
events.notes: Take water bottle. Chicken thighs thawing; avoid lunch stop after insurance draft clears.

events.title: Hefner path with Sam
events.notes: Flat stretch only. Check arm-cuff numbers before leaving. Gloves in jacket pocket if hands are slow.

events.title: Print order pickup
events.notes: Ask for matte finish on Flint Hills ridge and the red cliff pair. Check whether the wide grass shot needs less blue before ordering 8x10.

events.title: Move camera card files
events.notes: Make folders: 2026-03-16 Arcadia; 2026-03-18 pantry repair. Put second copy on gray Seagate if it is still plugged in.

events.title: Batch soup before errands
events.notes: Use turkey necks, okra, tomatoes. Freeze 3 tubs. Leave room Friday if Earl still wants lunch after chess; split one basket.

events.title: Haney call, then inventory list
events.notes: Milk, crackers, canned peaches. Ask about porch light. Text Jim counts before 5:00.

events.title: Primer coat - Bel Air shell
events.notes: After tax envelope. Clamp doors flat, use toothpick for trim line, no radio.

events.title: Meet Sam before sunrise
events.notes: Thermos, folding chair, bait bucket. Text Earl if back in time for afternoon board.

events.title: Bank: Vanguard draw
events.notes: $620 to checking. March cushion now about $2,463 with Treasury line; leave $225 for groceries, pharmacy, and gas.

events.title: Credit union: transfer for house drafts
events.location: Tinker Federal Credit Union, Oklahoma City
events.notes: Move $625 before mortgage escrow and utilities pull. Stop by HobbyTown for thin cement if the balance looks right.

events.title: Call Dr. Henson nurse line
events.notes: Ask whether to use county health department times or Walgreens walk-in for the next dose. Do not use the chart from Earl's forwarded post.

events.title: Porch box and ledger
events.notes: Rotate flashlight batteries. Count envelope: 20s and 5s. Confirm checking buffer still clears the 400 note before bill pay.

events.title: Ramp boards and fellowship hall sink
events.notes: Bring printed names, supply page, receipt envelope, and toolbox list. Check off lumber, pipe wrench, drill batteries, and petty cash purchases before lunch.

events.title: Church ramp supply check
events.notes: Measure rails, check deck boards, bring level, extra screws, trim pieces. Ask Jim if the old Cline crew photo can go in the outreach display with the Class of '65 program.

events.title: Set bean poles; thin lettuce; check blooms by fence
events.notes: Brace first if kneeling. Stool under shade tree. Water peppers at base, skip lettuce unless top inch is dry.

events.title: Recheck county guide before Tuesday
events.notes: Confirm precinct hours. Review sheriff staffing item, bridge repair question, and the two judicial pages. Do not use flyer alone; check OCPA notes and county minutes.

events.title: Repair day: doors, ramps, outlet checks
events.location: Church basement, then two houses near NW 23rd St
events.notes: Load folding table, cord labels, knee pads, hinge kit, and printed checklist. Call center office by 3:30 with head count for next Wednesday.

events.title: Karen call - Friday lake timing
